knownIssuesAndCaveats: The GitHub repository is public, so operational details already committed in docs/handoffs are externally visible even when they are not secret values.
A prior tracked handoff states that the Mac account password was exposed in a chat image. Rotate that password if it has not already been changed.
No external gitleaks/trufflehog binary was installed in this environment; the audit used a local redacted scanner with common high-signal detectors.
doNotRevertOrTouchWithoutUserRequest: Do not remove the new .gitignore local-secret guardrails unless replacing them with stronger secret hygiene.
Do not commit local .vercel auth material, SSH private keys, .env files, .npmrc, .netrc, .aws/, node_modules, dist, or browser save data.
recommendedNextSteps: Rotate the Mac account password if the previously noted exposure has not been handled.
Consider enabling GitHub push protection or an equivalent secret-scanning check in CI for defense in depth.
Optionally run gitleaks or trufflehog in a separate environment for a second scanner opinion before the next public push.
